title: Frontend: Flatten Nested Objects
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Flatten Nested Objects. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(value). Flatten nonempty plain nested JSON objects into sorted [dotPath,leaf] pairs. Arrays, null and empty objects are leaves. Keys do not contain dots. Output paths sort in ASCII order.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Walk own enumerable keys, accumulate a path, and emit non-plain-object leaves.
alternativeApproaches: Add an inverse unflatten operation and demonstrate why ambiguous separator encoding prevents a reliable round trip.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty object; array leaf; key containing a dot.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
